(I-VT.) criticized America’s worsening housing affordability crisis, citing million-dollar starter homes in 242 U.S. cities and urging the government to prioritize domestic housing needs over overseas military spending.
Sanders Highlights Rising Homeownership Barriers
On Saturday, in a post on
X
, Sanders highlighted the growing financial barriers facing Americans trying to purchase their first homes.
“In the richest country on Earth, starter homes now cost $1 million in a record 242 U.S. cities,” he wrote.
He also pointed to the rising age of first-time homebuyers, saying the median age has reached 40, up from 28 in the early 1990s.
“Unacceptable,” Sanders added, arguing that the government should redirect its spending priorities toward domestic needs.
“Instead of investing in endless wars, we should invest in affordable housing,” he wrote.
